scopeSummary: Blind source discovery from the two supplementary start regions at commit 33341eb227ab213b011868c9bc5c5f735aaaf875: desktop extension test configuration and selected chat tests, followed to eligible accessibility, transcript search, and automatic instruction implementations. All interpretations remain candidates.

omissions: Both assigned start regions were inspected; the chat test directory was sampled rather than exhaustively covered.

The broker rejected src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/actions/chatQueueActions.ts as ineligible. It was not retried through another path; queue and steering claims remain limited to inspected test assertions.
No extension test runner implementation, launched installation, generated reports, or extension test outcomes were inspected.
Accessibility action registration, full response navigation, and screen-reader interaction were not inspected.
Transcript Find UI highlighting and getChatFindTextParts implementation were not inspected.
Prompt file enumeration, customizations index construction, and the complete referenced-file traversal were not inspected because the serialized receipt budget was nearly exhausted.

crossPartitionLeads: The inspected .vscode-test.js is in partition C and configures desktop test launches through scripts/code.sh or scripts/code.bat or an installation override; those launcher implementations remain uninspected.
Automatic instruction attachment consumes results from the prompts service and mutates chat request variables; broader enumeration and request delivery responsibilities require separate evidence.
Accessible response text and transcript Find both consume chat response models but use different content-selection paths; avoid equating their treatment of thinking and tool content.

nodes.name: Configure desktop extension integration test runs
nodes.summary: Build per-extension test configurations with workspace selection, test files, launch settings, and conditional CI reports.
nodes.actor: Repository developer or CI test invoker
inputs: Environment overrides for launch arguments and installation path
CI workspace or artifact staging environment
outcomes: Exported test configurations for desktop extension suites
Default test-file and development-path selection with per-suite overrides
Conditional specification and JUnit report configuration
conditions: The listed extension must have a configuration entry
Desktop configurations receive launch arguments and an installation path
CI reporting is configured when BUILD_ARTIFACTSTAGINGDIRECTORY or GITHUB_WORKSPACE is present
exclusions: Web configurations are not implemented in the inspected branch
Configuration does not establish that any suite executed or passed
uncertainty: Runner interpretation and actual launches were not observed

claims.text: The configuration derives desktop test file globs and extension development paths, while allowing suite entries to override them and supply workspaces and Mocha options.

Desktop launches receive configured arguments, an environment-selectable installation path, and VSCODE_SKIP_PRELAUNCH; CI environments additionally configure spec and JUnit reporters with platform-specific report paths.

nodes.name: Choose queued or steering chat follow-ups
nodes.summary: Candidate input responsibility for sending follow-up text during an active chat request, with configurable keyboard choice and a hidden-request exception evidenced by test assertions.
nodes.actor: Chat user entering a follow-up during an active request
inputs: Default action setting of steer or queue
Whether the active request is hidden from the transcript
outcomes: Expected Enter and Alt+Enter bindings select queue or steer according to the default
Expected steering action submits queued mode behind a hidden active request
conditions: Inspected keybinding tests enable input text, chat input focus, and request-in-progress context
Inspected action tests use a stubbed widget and chat model
exclusions: Queue ordering, processing, cancellation, and provider steering behavior are not established
Side-chat action behavior was not inspected beyond its suite declaration
uncertainty: The imported action implementation was rejected by the broker
Tests were read but not executed; assertions express expected behavior

claims.text: The inspected tests assert that default=steer maps Enter to steering and Alt+Enter to queueing, and default=queue reverses those bindings.
The inspected stubbed action test expects hidden active requests to receive Queued follow-ups and visible active requests to receive Steering follow-ups.
These assertions suggest a user-facing follow-up mode choice with hidden-request protection, but implementation behavior remains unconfirmed.

nodes.name: Read chat responses as accessible text
nodes.summary: Provide ordered plaintext descriptions of response content and tool states to the accessible chat view, refreshing when response data or thinking inclusion settings change.
nodes.actor: Chat user consuming the accessible response view
inputs: Response content parts and tool invocation states
outcomes: Plaintext response content with blank lines removed
Text descriptions of confirmations, authentication requests, post-approval results, references, and completed or active tools
Content-change notifications and restoration of input or item focus on close
conditions: The accessible provider returns empty content for non-response items
Thinking text is included only when requested by the inclusion preference
Some output branches depend on tool state and response completion
exclusions: No proof of screen-reader announcements or rendered accessibility interaction
No assertion that every response-part kind produces text
uncertainty: Accessible view registration and full previous/next navigation were outside inspected windows
Underlying formatting helpers were not inspected

claims.text: The provider subscribes to response-model and thinking-preference changes, derives text from response parts, removes blank lines, and restores input or item focus on close.

The plaintext extractor handles Markdown, optional thinking, notification accessibility labels, references, elicitation prompts, and tool confirmation, authentication, post-approval, and completion states.
Tests assert precedence of user-edited over tool-edited over original terminal commands in descriptive text; the inspected extraction implementation delegates tool-specific descriptions to a helper.

nodes.name: Find and navigate text in a chat transcript
nodes.summary: Build query matches over logical request and response segments, order matches newest first, and preserve or choose an active location for navigation.
inputs: Query text and regex, case, and whole-word options
outcomes: Ordered matches with item, part, occurrence, and text offsets
Next and previous match navigation with wraparound
Invalid-regex state or cleared matches for empty queries
Preserved active match when its anchor survives recomputation
conditions: Response segments are mapped to rendered content parts
Match collection is capped and individual segment scans are bounded
Viewport-relative initial selection is used when no surviving active match exists
exclusions: Inspected tests exclude reasoning and tool invocations from searchable matches
Actual DOM highlighting and scrolling were not inspected
This is not evidence of repository-wide file search
uncertainty: getChatFindTextParts was called in inspected code but its own implementation was not read
UI wiring and execution were not verified

claims.text: The inspected implementation creates bounded matches from logical transcript segments, records item and rendered-part coordinates, and gathers occurrences newest first.

Query compilation honors regex, case, and whole-word options; invalid expressions clear matches and set invalid-regex state. Next and previous navigation wrap, and recomputation can preserve an existing match anchor or seed from the viewport.
Tests assert matches across request and response Markdown while excluding thinking and tool invocations; this narrows transcript Find relative to the accessible response text extractor.

nodes.name: Attach applicable instruction files to chat requests
nodes.summary: Enrich chat request variables with applicable instruction-file references and agent instructions, using attached-file patterns, session type, and configuration gates.
nodes.actor: Chat request preparation subsystem acting on user and workspace customizations
inputs: Existing chat request variables and attached file URIs
Instruction candidates from the prompts service
Instruction applyTo or paths patterns and session-type restrictions
Configuration, chat mode, and cancellation token
outcomes: Added instruction-file variables with reasons for automatic attachment
Agent instruction variables included from prompts-service candidates
Collection counts and diagnostic reasons for attached or skipped candidates
conditions: Applying instructions are gated by configuration except in Edit mode
Instructions without patterns, with incompatible session types, or already present in the input context are skipped
Special wildcard patterns can attach instructions without attached files
Matching is case-insensitive and supports comma-separated glob patterns
exclusions: Attachment does not establish model compliance with instructions
Instruction-file enumeration and trusted-source filtering were not inspected
Complete recursive reference behavior and customization index content are not established
uncertainty: The inspected test window primarily establishes setup and imports rather than successful behavioral assertions
Reference traversal was inspected only through initialization and the beginning of reference parsing
Downstream request dispatch was not inspected

claims.text: Collection invokes applying-instruction selection, referenced-instruction processing, agent-instruction addition, and optional customization-index addition before recording collection diagnostics.

Applying selection checks configuration and Edit mode, session type, pattern presence, and existing context, then adds instruction variables with match reasons. The matcher supports universal wildcards, relative patterns, comma-separated patterns, and case-insensitive attached-file matching.
Agent-instruction candidates returned by the prompts service are added as instruction variables; copilot instruction entries also pass through referenced-instruction processing.

Referenced-instruction processing is configuration-gated except in Edit mode and initializes a deduplicated worklist from attached prompt-file variables; its complete traversal and attachment behavior remain outside the read window.

edges.reason: Both derive readable content from chat responses, but the accessible extractor includes optional thinking and detailed tool states while the inspected Find assertions exclude thinking and tool invocations. Shared response subject matter does not make the experiences identical or establish a direct implementation dependency.

limitations: Source inspection supports candidate implementation responsibilities, not independent verification or runtime guarantees.
No target code was executed, no network or paid APIs were used, and no workers were spawned.
Used 12 successful source windows and 3 searches. Retrieval stopped near the 72000-byte serialized receipt cap, before exhausting the window count.
One implementation read was rejected as ineligible and was not retried. Test assertions on that branch are explicitly distinguished from inspected implementation.
Search receipts were used only for navigation; all claims and relationships cite inspected source receipts.
The chat test directory has hundreds of files; inspected branches do not establish full regional coverage or the absence of other responsibilities.
No baseline, prior proposals, historical maps, owner feedback, or review labels were consulted. No fixed hierarchy or target capability count was imposed.
